1686-12-05.summary: Battier, Dutch envoy extraordinary in Madrid, to Grand Pensionary Gaspar Fagel; a contemporary decipherment survives on scan 28R and is transcribed beside the key reading as a validation.
1686-12-05.en:
The court intrigues still stand on the same terms; yet it seems that the Count of Oropesa will not yet become first
minister, partly because his confessor advises him against it, and partly because this King is not much inclined to
it either; meanwhile all public business remains undone, because there is no one who looks after more than his own
interests. He may well become Master of the Horse, but then he would have to give up the presidency of the Realm of
Castile, and if Cardinal Salazar became president and chief, the Count of Oropesa would not much like it; how they will
still turn it, I shall make known to Your Honour in future.

From all sides it is written that France and England are still deliberating in what way they can most conveniently make
war on the State;

1686-12-19.summary: Battier to Fagel; the four numbered passages deciphered by a contemporary clerk on scan 32R make this letter the third validation of the key against contemporary plaintext.
1686-12-19.en:
⟨Right Honourable Sir, My Lord. For the Netherlands nothing has yet been resolved, nor can it be until a good sum of
money is found ... Nor is it known whether one of the said three will obtain the governorship. The Count of Melgar had
good hopes, but since then the Admiral has written to Don Manuel de Lira in such terms about his son's disgrace that the
King is very ill pleased with it. Now there is also talk of the Marquis of Leganés, and some speak⟩ of the Count of
Mansfeld; but since this last once failed, his person is little esteemed and his credit here at court very slight, and
therefore there is little likelihood for him either.

⟨The Count of Oropesa remains in great credit; the King's confessor, who was not his friend, has asked for and obtained
his dismissal, and another has already been named;⟩ but for all that public business is not done, and everything goes
on dragging.

1687-01-30.summary: Battier to Fagel; the contemporary decipherment on scans 42R-43R (file misdated 16 Jan) deciphers this one letter and is transcribed beside the key reading.
1687-01-30.en:
My Lord. Since the last post I have consulted with Cantelmo how best to work for Castañaga, and we have thought it good
to do it underhand, for otherwise it could be harmful to Castañaga, because [?they] are so touchy here and do not want
their neighbours to meddle in their domestic affairs. The Emperor's ambassador has already spoken of it openly
everywhere, and the Master of the Horse of Aureis came to tell me that he had heard, on a visit of consequence, that His
Highness had written in Castañaga's favour, and that it was taken ill. I merely answered that I knew nothing of it, for I
noticed that he had come to sound me out in order to report back to the Emperor's ambassador. I have nevertheless done my
duty wherever I thought it necessary. Monterrey assures me that, to his knowledge, nothing has yet been resolved, and
perhaps will not be resolved so soon either.

1687-04-24.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid, with no known contemporary decipherment: Gastanaga may be removed before the end of his three years or employed in Peru or Catalonia; the Emperor's ambassador moves heaven and earth to regain the Queen's good grace, working through a nun, the confessor and ministers, but Battier thinks the Queen will never forget the harm he did her.
1687-04-24.en:
⟨Right Honourable Sir, My Lord. I have nothing else by this post than that the Duke of Arco has gone back to Brussels;
Mr vander Hagen has also gone with him ... Before his departure he informed the Count of Melgar about it at length; and
some therefore wish to judge that there would now again be great likelihood of making the said Count succeed the Marquis
of Gastañaga,⟩ but I can assure Your Honour that, if he gives Castañaga wholly new cause for complaint, since Her Majesty
will remove him before the end of the three years, or they might wish to employ him in Peru or Catalonia.

The Emperor's ambassador still does everything he can to have the same profit as his predecessor had, and moves heaven
and earth to come back into the Queen's good gra[ce]; but there is very little, or better said, absolutely not the
least likelihood of it, as with the King;

1687-12-04.summary: Battier to Fagel; the clear close on 92R reports that Leganés wants service and lodging money for 14 men and that the Prince of Parma has arrived with a train of 140 persons.
1687-12-04.en:
It is now absolutely intended that the government of the Netherlands shall be deliberated upon; that the Count of Melgar
and the Marquis of Leganés would be the nearest to it, and that, if Leganés prevails, the Marquis of Gastañaga would then
receive the viceroyalty of Catalonia; but all without the least certainty. On the contrary, Monsieur Novelli [is]
sounding out [the post of] Hofmeister for the son of the Palatinate, and [?expects] further work [from the] Elector
Palatine [...] [?armed].

The Spaniards have so far not wished to show their hand much, so as not to be obliged to improve the conditions, and the
Palatinate for its part will form no claim, for fear that no advantage would then be obtained;

1688-01-29.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid; no contemporary decipherment recorded.
1688-01-29.en:
⟨Of the government of the Netherlands there is now very little talk, and the friends of the Marquis of Gastañaga hope
that His Excellency will be continued for three more years. But since by this post the Elector Palatine offers Mr
Novelli the ministry at this court, and says he will send letters of credence to His Honour by the next post, it is easy
to presume that⟩ the Grand Master's pretension is not yet entirely [?], which I shall surely learn from him ⟨when his
letters of credence and his instructions come. Meanwhile the⟩ guard Don Marcos de Velasco has also [?] [?], and offers
[?] rixdollars for it; ⟨likewise yet another gentleman presents himself⟩ who is willing to give a [?] sum. ⟨But before he
makes any effective suit, they will not tell me his name ...⟩

1688-02-12.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid; separate decipherment sheets near this letter have not been checked.
1688-02-12.en:
Sir. Since my most humble last letter I have read the letter that the Count Palatine wrote to Monsieur Novelli on behalf
of the Grand Master, to this effect: His Electoral Highness orders him to sound out on what footing and conditions His
Majesty would hand over the government of Flanders to his son, and His Electoral Highness hoped that the last [431] [374]
[137] [512] would have brought his son into [604] reputation and credit, so that His Majesty would also take it into
account.

1688-02-26.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid, partly deciphered interlinear at the time (scan 101R).
1688-02-26.en:
My Lord. With the Grand Master ⟨everything still stands as it was, because the Imperial letters⟩ which have been sent off
at Heidelberg ⟨are awaited first; but as soon as they come, the matter will be put to deliberation and His Imperial
Majesty answered. Meanwhile the gentleman has desisted from his pretension, because he has learned that⟩ the Grand
Master would stand in his way. ⟨Nevertheless, because some imagine that now that it is almost public⟩ the Marquis will
oppose it, and [?] ⟨so as to resolve all the sooner to take another, as if one⟩ still had [given] it to the Grand
Master; so the [?] Duke of Holstein also offers himself, who also offers [?] rixdollars ⟨and [says] that he knows means to
maintain 25,000 men without getting money from Spain; and it seems that Robiano ...⟩

1688-04-08.summary: Battier to Fagel from Madrid, with no contemporary decipherment: the Grand Maestre has ordered his agent to reassure the old Queen, and a sworn party forms against him (the Constable of Castile, Os[t]una and Monterey?); the reviewed reconstruction (codex_review/april_reading.md) supersedes the earlier fluent reading.
1688-04-08.en:
⟨Since the last post ... the Bishop of Breslau and the High Marshal sent to Vienna ... and by this last post⟩ the Grand
Master has ordered his agent to assure the old Queen ⟨that in 14 days without fail the Imperial letters would be here ...
I fear that our slowness will give⟩ Oropesa ⟨time to get ahead of us.⟩ Melgar is still soliciting, and so ⟨Leganés ...⟩

⟨Count Cifuentes, to whom⟩ only so as to be able to make Altamira viceroy of [?] ⟨they had given the viceroyalty of Peru
... Don Gaspar de Silva, Viceroy of Mexico⟩ — Spanish thrift now shows itself here clearly. ⟨Portocarrero has cut His
Majesty short by 60,000 pieces of eight ... No money will be remitted to the Netherlands⟩ as long as Castañaga remains
governor;

1687-01-02.summary: Battier to Fagel: nobody at court thinks of remedying affairs; the King could not find a thousand pistoles for the Queen's New Year; Spain will not let its neighbours force it to change the pragmatic, yet will have to.
1687-01-02.en:
Sir. The affairs of this court remain in a state, that is to say in [?a] [703], and there is nobody who thinks of
remedying them.

Last Thursday a new governor for the Netherlands was to be chosen, but for lack of money it was not done: 160 thousand
pieces of eight have arrived here from Seville, yet it seems that the King has the least share of them; for His Majesty,
who wished to give the Queen a thousand pistoles for the New Year, could not find so much, [?but] not four hundred pistoles
for [?her] [?person]. [361] [448] [the] widow, whom His Majesty has had already for six [?years] [...], still it is not to
be [?understood] [...] all [?affairs] [...] [409].

[36L] [...] and also that one does not willingly let oneself be forced by the neighbours to change the pragmatic; none
the less I firmly believe that they will [?also] have to do it all.

1687-03-13a.summary: Oropesa is to speak for Cogolludo, Melgar and Balbases: Cogolludo's son to be sent to Rome and Naples, Melgar if that fails, Balbases to get him away.
1687-03-13a.en:
But it is intended that Oropesa shall also speak for Cogolludo, for Melgar and for Balbases: for Cogolludo, so as
then to content Melgar's father, yet to send the son to Rome and [886] to send him the way to Naples; for Melgar, if the
first does not come off; and for Balbases, if [?both] do not come off, to get him away.

1687-03-13b.summary: The Empress says it matters little whether Spain, in so poor a state, joins or not; for the consequence Spain will not be brought to it.
1687-03-13b.en:
the Empress says that it matters little whether Spain, which is in any case in so poor a state, [888] itself
with it or not; but for the sake of the consequence Spain will not let itself be brought to it.

1687-06-10.summary: One is oppressed on all sides and cannot act against the subjects (67L; 67R is WAINUT's).

1687-07.summary: One could not be content with the declaration and must insist in England; agreement with the articles of the Indies; the explanation to the Emperor.
1687-07.en:
Today the King's thoughts are [...] that one could namely not be content with this declaration, and must insist in
England, to be encouraged [e] and to agree with the articles of the Indies, to have the explanation, to His Imperial
[Majesty] [...]

1687-08.summary: The Hofmeister is very changeable and will have trouble maintaining himself unless the Jesuits make it their business.

1687-09-11.summary: The President and the Constable of Castile, formerly against him, now speak for him, since Spain is thinking of the son of the Palatine.
1687-09-11.en:
and [260] [117] are still [?struck] and [779] the Palatinate [60].

There is [...] and that even the President of Castile and the Constable of Castile, who were most against him, now speak
for him; indeed it is said that, since Spain is thinking of the son of the Palatine, some have written to Brussels [...]

1687-09-25.summary: Letters from Vienna and the Palatinate delayed; if the Emperor proposed the Palatine's son Spain would agree; if Medinaceli came in by one gate, [the President of Castile] would go out by another.

1687-12-18.summary: The Grand Master wrote to his agent Don Pedro Alvares that he would go to Vienna; he was unwell and could not follow the Emperor to Pressburg; he is thought to hold back on the Netherlands to see whether he gets the presidency of the war council.
1687-12-18.en:
Sir. Eight days ago, by the Italian post, the Grand Master wrote from [888] [oa] to his agent Don Pedro Alvares, who
had made the first attempt in his name and had received as answer from Don M. de Lira that, if the proposal were made by
the Emperor, His Majesty would then take the matter into consideration, that His Highness, after his regiment had gone
into winter quarters, would go [178] by post to Vienna and seek to dispose [?the Emperor] to it.

But by the last Flanders post one has learnt that His Highness was indeed at Vienna [883], but found himself somewhat
unwell, and therefore had not been able to follow the Emperor to Pressburg, [?so] that His Highness would write more
fully by the next post.

1687-12-18b.summary: French refugees: Mr Schonenberg; the main cause; orders given. Letter runs in part only.

1688-01-01.summary: Battier could not learn what the Grand Master [did] by this post, the holy days having prevented him from speaking to everyone.
1688-01-01.en:
I have not been able to learn what the Grand Master [861] by this post, for the holy days have prevented one from
speaking to everyone.

1688-01-29b.summary: 60 thousand guilders, not pounds Flemish; the confessor, Nuñez Botello and Carnero did most; the Councils made no mention of the money.

1688-02-26b.summary: The confessor, a Theatine; conferences with ministers on behalf of the Grand Master.

1688-03-11.summary: The Grand Master affair is off again; Melgar offers money; the Duke of Holstein desists; or the Grand Master is to marry the Infanta and receive the government of the Netherlands.
1688-03-11.en:
Yesterday I was given to believe that it is off again with the Grand Master, that the Count of Melgar is now also
offering a sum of money, and that the Duke of Holstein therefore desists, fearing not to obtain it; but since it is also
said that the Spanish ambassador at Lisbon is corresponding with Mr Novelly and proposing to Prince Charles to cede the
Grand Mastership, or else to ask a dispensation from the Pope for the Grand Master to marry the Infanta, and to entrust
him with the government of the Netherlands, I cannot yet tell Your Honour exactly which of the two is true.

snip.cap: 8 April 1688, right page: the cipher after “voor den Opperstal Meester te vinden syn” describes a sworn party; Osuna remains speculative.

system: A Dutch homophonic letter table accompanies an alphabetical codebook with fifteen marked number series and names.
